title: The ば / れば conditional
summary: ば is the hypothetical "if". Its hypothetical nature gives you advice (どうすればいい), regret (ばよかった) and obligation (なければいけない).

blocks.text: Where と says "this always leads to that", **ば** (also called れば) says **"suppose this"**. It is always "if", never "when", because it states a hypothesis, not a fact.
ば is a helper that sits on the え-stem (the stem from lesson 7.5: 行く → 行け). Ichidan verbs drop る and take れば, and adjectives follow the same pattern as くない, かった, ければ.

rows: しない → しなければ

blocks.text: Hypothetical, so not about what happened
Because ば only supposes, using it about the past means the thing did **not** happen. That is the reason ばよかった is regret: "if I had done it, it would have been good (but I did not)".
Three expressions that come from hypotheticals
Japanese has no single word for "should" or "must". It uses a hypothetical instead, and that is why ば appears in so many set phrases. Think of する as "act" here.
**どうすればいい?** is literally "if I act how, would it be good?", which is "What should I do?"

blocks.jp: どうすればいいですか。

blocks.text: **〜ばよかった** is "if I had done it, it would have been good", which is regret: "I should have".

blocks.jp: 傘を持ってくればよかった。
blocks.en: I should have brought an umbrella.

blocks.text: **〜なければいけない** unpacks like this: しなければ is "if I do not do it", and いけない is "it will not do". Together: "I must". Lesson 30 had the same idea with と (しないといけない); this is the ば version. Casually the end is dropped: **〜なきゃ**.
勉強しなければいけない。 I have to study.

blocks.jp: もう行かなければいけない。

blocks.en: I have to go to bed early.

items: **どうすればいい**: what should I do?
**〜ばよかった**: I should have / I wish I had.
**〜なければいけない / 〜なきゃ**: must.

questions.instruction: Pick the ば form of 飲む
questions.note: Godan: え-stem + ば.

questions.instruction: Pick the ば form of 見る
questions.note: Ichidan: drop る, add れば.

questions.instruction: Pick the ば form of 安い
questions.note: Drop い, add ければ.

questions.instruction: Pick the ば form of 読まない
questions.note: ない works like an い-adjective: なければ.

questions.prompt: もっと早く起きればよかった。
options: I should have gotten up earlier
I will get up early tomorrow
I do not need to get up early
questions.note: ばよかった: regret.
questions.en: I should have gotten up earlier.

questions.prompt: この薬を飲めば、すぐ治りますよ。
options: A hypothesis: if you take it
questions.note: ば is hypothetical.
questions.en: If you take this medicine, you'll get better soon.

questions.prompt: 明日までに宿題を出さなければいけません。
options: I must not hand it in
I have to hand in my homework by tomorrow
questions.note: なければいけない: must.
questions.en: I have to hand in my homework by tomorrow.

questions.prompt: 友達に聞けばよかった。
questions.note: ば + よかった: it would have been good.
questions.en: I should have asked my friend.

questions.prompt: 駅までどう行けばいいですか。
options: How did you get to the station?
How should I get to the station?
I got to the station somehow
questions.note: どうすればいい: what should I do?
questions.en: How should I get to the station?

questions.prompt: もっと勉強すれ＿＿よかった。
questions.note: ば + よかった: regret.

questions.prompt: お金がなけれ＿＿、買えない。
questions.note: なければ: if there is not.
questions.en: If I have no money, I cannot buy it.

questions.prompt: ば is used for something certain to happen at a known time.
questions.note: ば is always hypothetical: if.

questions.instruction: What does 寝なきゃ stand for?
questions.note: なければ shrinks to なきゃ.

questions.instruction: Which sentence says "I should not have said that"?
options: 言わなければよかった。
言わなければいけない。
questions.note: Negative ば + よかった.

options: 寒ければ、ストーブをつける。
寒いば、ストーブをつける。
questions.note: い-adjectives use ければ.

questions.instruction: What does どうすればいい literally ask?
options: If I act how, would it be good?
questions.note: する = act: if I act how is it good.

questions.prompt: If you go by taxi, you can make it in time.
questions.note: Hypothetical clause, then result.
questions.en: If you go by taxi, you can make it in time.

questions.note: ば + よかった.

questions.prompt: I have to wash the dishes.
questions.note: なければいけない.
questions.en: I have to wash the dishes.

questions.prompt: If this book is cheap, I will buy it.
questions.note: い-adjective: ければ.
questions.en: If this book is cheap, I will buy it.

questions.instruction: Tap the part that says "it would have been good"
questions.note: Past よかった: it would have been good.
questions.en: I should have studied a little more.

questions.note: なければ: if we do not.
questions.en: If we don't hurry, we won't make the train.

questions.instruction: What does ば tell you about the past here?
options: I did not go to bed early
I always go to bed early
I will go to bed early
questions.note: ば is hypothetical: used about the past, it means it did not happen.
questions.en: I should have gone to bed early.
